messages.subject: Multiple Groups No Standard Error
parts:
Hello, I am trying to run a Monte Carlo. Having generated the dataset I am analyzing it with the same model (i.e. no misspec), however standard errors (and robust fit indices) are not being calculated. The parameter estimates otherwise are fairly accurate.

I have been through other posts and assume I must be missing some identification conditions for my comparison group but I can't for the life of me figure out what I am missing. I am attempting to replicate an MPlus study that worked fine, and the parameters are identical (unless there are some default MPlus parameters I am missing):

simple.spec.2<-'

f1 =~ 0.85*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6
f2 =~ 0.55*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4

f2 ~ f1

f1 ~ c(0,NA)*1
f2 ~ c(0,NA)*1

x1 ~~ c(1,NA)*x1
x2 ~~ c(1,NA)*x2
x3 ~~ c(1,NA)*x3
x4 ~~ c(1,NA)*x4
x5 ~~ c(1,NA)*x5
x6 ~~ c(1,NA)*x6

x1 | t1 + t2
x2 | t1 + t2
x3 | t1 + t2
x4 | t1 + t2
x5 | t1 + t2
x6 | t1 + t2

y1 ~~ c(1,NA)*y1
y2 ~~ c(1,NA)*y2
y3 ~~ c(1,NA)*y3
y4 ~~ c(1,NA)*y4

y1 | t1 + t2 + t3 + t4
y2 | t1 + t2 + t3 + t4
y3 | t1 + t2 + t3 + t4
y4 | t1 + t2 + t3 + t4

'
t<-sem(model=simple.spec.2,data=data,parameterization = "theta",group="group")


Can anyone point out what I am doing wrong?

P.s. When I transfer the syntax to the simsem "sim" function it goes even one further and totally refuses to converge.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Groups No Standard Error
parts:
On 04/01/2015 10:29 PM, UCLU wrote:
> life of me figure out what I am missing. I am attempting to replicate an
> MPlus study that worked fine, and the parameters are identical (unless
> there are some default MPlus parameters I am missing):

If you still have the Mplus files, look at the output of TECH1, and
compare this with the output of inspect(fit), to see which parameters
are free/fixed in Mplus/lavaan.

For the output below, I believe the problem is:

You free up the latent means of the second group, but that requires that
at least two thresholds of the indicators are fixed. Or, if you can
assume strong invariance, you can restrict all thresholds of the
indicators to be the same in both groups.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Multiple Groups No Standard Error
parts:
Hi Yves,

Many thanks for this. I snooped around the TECH1 documentation and indeed it helped.

It turns out MPlus implicitly specifies group parameters to be equal unless it is explicitly stated otherwise. So resolving the problem was simply a matter of forcing equality across all parameters, and only freeing those I knew had non-invariance it my specified population. If it helps anyone else, the modified script is:

model1<-'


f1 =~ 0.85*x1 + x2 + c(l1.3,l1.3)*x3 + x4 + c(l1.5,l1.5)*x5 + x6
f2 =~ 0.55*y1 + c(l2.2,l2.2)*y2 + c(l2.3,l2.3)*y3 + c(l2.4,l2.4)*y4


f2 ~ f1

f1 ~~ f1
f2 ~~ f2


x1 ~~ c(1,NA)*x1
x2 ~~ c(1,1)*x2
x3 ~~ c(1,NA)*x3
x4 ~~ c(1,1)*x4
x5 ~~ c(1,NA)*x5
x6 ~~ c(1,1)*x6


x1 | c(a,a)*t1 + c(b,b)*t2
x2 | t1 + t2
x3 | c(c,c)*t1 + c(d,d)*t2
x4 | t1 + t2
x5 | c(e,e)*t1 + c(f,f)*t2

x6 | t1 + t2


y1 ~~ c(1,NA)*y1
y2 ~~ c(1,NA)*y2
y3 ~~ c(1,NA)*y3
y4 ~~ c(1,NA)*y4

y1 | c(g,g)*t1 + c(h,h)*t2 + c(i,i)*t3 + c(j,j)*t4
y2 | c(k,k)*t1 + c(l,l)*t2 + c(m,m)*t3 + c(n,n)*t4
y3 | c(o,o)*t1 + c(p,p)*t2 + c(q,q)*t3 + c(r,r)*t4
y4 | c(s,s)*t1 + c(t,t)*t2 + c(u,u)*t3 + c(v,v)*t4


'
